original_question: Does the mapping class group of a closed surface have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap, that is, must every faithful action of that group on a set X have Vol_{G,X}(n) bounded below by some superlinear function up to the paper's asymptotic comparison?
target_in_paper: Question 6.4 in Section 6: "Does the mapping class group of a closed surface have nontrivial Schreier growth gap?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's exact target. It identifies the right group (the mapping class group of a closed surface), the right property (having a nontrivial Schreier growth gap), and the right universal flavor of the question (a lower bound that must hold for every faithful action on a set). It also correctly interprets the question as asking for a superlinear lower bound in the paper's asymptotic sense.
missing_details: The paper's official formulation is the one-line Question 6.4 in Section 6; your draft should explicitly align with that label rather than the broader neighboring hyperbolic-group questions.

The action-growth function needs to be defined: vol_{G,X}(n) is the size of the largest radius-n ball in the Schreier graph of the action, equivalently max_{x in X} |B_S(n)·x| for a finite generating set S of G.
The action on X is not assumed transitive, so the Schreier graph may be disconnected; this is why one takes the largest ball over all vertices x in X.
A Schreier growth gap means there exists a single function f, depending only on G, that works uniformly for every faithful G-set X; the lower bound is not allowed to vary with X.
The asymptotic comparison should be stated explicitly: h preccurlyeq k means there exists C > 0 such that h(n) <= C k(Cn) for all n >= 1, and h succcurlyeq k is the reverse relation.
It helps to note that the definition is independent of the chosen finite generating set up to the paper's asymptotic equivalence.
The paper's term 'nontrivial' is attached to a superlinear lower bound; your draft should state that this is the sense in which the gap is nontrivial.

To make the question fully stand-alone, the ambient mapping class group should be named explicitly, e.g. Mod(Sigma_g) for a closed orientable surface; in the intended nontrivial case one usually has g >= 2.
refined_question: Let G = Mod(Sigma_g) be the mapping class group of a closed orientable surface Sigma_g (in the intended nontrivial case, g >= 2), and fix a finite generating set S of G. For a faithful action G acting on a set X, define vol_{G,X}(n) := max_{x in X} |B_S(n)·x|, i.e. the cardinality of the largest radius-n ball in the possibly disconnected Schreier graph of the action. Does there exist a superlinear function f: N -> N such that every faithful G-set X satisfies vol_{G,X}(n) succcurlyeq f(n), where h preccurlyeq k means that there exists C > 0 with h(n) <= C k(Cn) for all n >= 1?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the language of Definition 6.1, does the mapping class group of a closed surface have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap?
justification: The draft clearly targets Question 6.4, not the broader Questions 6.2 and 6.3 about hyperbolic groups in general. Section 6 first introduces the action-growth invariant vol_{G,X}(n) for faithful actions on sets and explains that, since transitivity is not assumed, one must measure the largest ball in the possibly disconnected Schreier graph. Definition 6.1 then defines what it means for a group to have a Schreier growth gap and when that gap is nontrivial. Question 6.4 is exactly the specialization of that framework to mapping class groups of closed surfaces, so the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply to unpack that definition in full and attach it to Mod(Sigma_g).

citations.label: Opening paragraph of Section 6 (definition of the action-growth function vol_{G,X}(n) and the Schreier-graph viewpoint)
